I'm digging into the reported bug about chats not resuming by session id, but the chat flow looks stateless since the caller passes history explicitly—none of the agents (triage, order, refund) seem to maintain a session store for chat specifically, only refundAgent has any store at all.

That mismatch—only refunds persisting state—would explain why order-status follow-ups fail while refund conversations work. I should search the repo for session handling patterns like sessionId or loadSession to find where this is actually wired up.

Only agents.ts even defines a session concept, and only refundAgent actually uses a store — triage and orderAgent both lack one, so their sessions stay in-memory only. That's likely the bug: when a customer mentions their order then asks a follow-up, triage delegates to orderAgent, but since neither persists session state, the context doesn't survive across reloads or separate processes.

I should check how genkit's defineAgent and the agents() middleware handle store config to confirm whether triage needs its own store to make session.get(id) work across requests.

This confirms only refundAgent has a store configured, so triage and orderAgent won't persist sessions via loadChat/sessionId since getSnapshot needs a server store. That means the "My order is A-1001" then "What is its status?" flow through triage delegating to orderAgent likely relies on the agents() middleware's historyLength instead of persisted session state.

The root cause looks like triage (and transitively orderAgent) is missing the store session configuration in src/agents.ts, so order-status chats can't be resumed by session id — only refundAgent has that. I want to check if orderAgent also needs its own store, or if it inherits context since it's invoked within triage's turn via the agents() middleware — let me look at the middleware's type definitions to confirm.

This confirms sub-agent delegation runs ephemerally within the orchestrator's turn, so persistence only needs to happen at the triage level — the fix is adding `store` to the triage agent definition so its session can persist and reload by session id. I'm now checking whether to reuse the same FileSessionStore instance used for refundAgent or give triage its own store directory.

Reusing the same instance should be fine since FileSessionStore partitions by snapshotId, so I'll just add store: store to triage and write the fix.
Let me verify this by building and typechecking.
Typechecks clean with no errors. Now let's write `answer.json`.

Root cause found and fixed: `triage` in `src/agents.ts` — the agent the support chat actually talks to — was defined without a session `store`, unlike `refundAgent`. Without a persistent store, its session state lives only in memory, so it can't be reloaded by session id on the follow-up turn, forcing the customer to restart. Fixed by adding `store` (the existing `FileSessionStore`) to the `triage` agent config, and wrote `answer.json` with the required details.
